When Mike has a release your copy doesn': When Mike has a release your copy doesn't have, Threadbear starts a thread that merges it in and runs the checks, then asks you before it lands. Never more than one at a time. A release Mike marks important doesn't wait.
When a thread changes code and is done,:
When a thread changes code and is done, another lab tries to break the change in a review thread of its own. Your thread waits for what it finds, fixes what holds up, and tells you in its reply.

A change gets one reviewer: the first in Every change that isn't the thread's own provider and has a login with room, so when one runs out the next takes over. Drag them to change the order. A big or risky change gets everyone in Big or risky changes at once, or one reviewer from Every change if fewer than two of them can review. With no other lab to hand, a fresh session of the thread's own provider reviews.
When you ask a thread to change Threadbe: When you ask a thread to change Threadbear, its agent can check this log first to see how you really use the app. It notes the buttons, rows and menu items you use (by their tooltips and titles), your shortcuts, the threads and pages you open, and when you send or answer something, never what you type. It stays on this Mac for 30 days and Threadbear never sends it anywhere.
